name: Forty Days in the Null Ward
description: Shot entirely on salvaged flat-panel rigs in Tier 1's flooded sub-basement districts, this 94-minute film follows a delirious BCI-withdrawal patient hallucinating her own past across fractured timelines. Director Celestine Abubakar-Johansson shot without permits over eighteen months, using non-actors recruited from the wards themselves. The film has no licensed distribution and exists only on physical drives and pirate mesh.
cultural_impact: Became a touchstone for the Shelf's flat-screen revival movement and is screened annually in semi-secret gatherings called the Null Vigils.
story_hooks: A journalist tracking the film's distribution network discovers it is being used as a dead drop container — the real data is steganographically embedded in the video file
Celestine Abubakar-Johansson has been missing since 2207 and her last known location was a Sable Charter medical facility
One of the non-actor subjects of the film approaches a player character, claiming the film captured something real about her past that she cannot otherwise remember
